name: Add SPEED_OF_LIGHT + BOLTZMANN_CONSTANT physical constants to std.units

task_definition.title: Add SPEED_OF_LIGHT + BOLTZMANN_CONSTANT physical constants to std.units
task_definition.description:
Complete the spec §11.3 std.units physical-constants promise (pi/g/c/boltzmann). Currently only STANDARD_GRAVITY() (=g) exists at units.ri:82; pi is a compiler builtin (constants.rs BUILTIN_NAMES); c and boltzmann are MISSING.

Append two zero-arg pub fn constants to crates/reify-compiler/stdlib/units.ri, in the existing STANDARD_GRAVITY() idiom (Reify lacks top-level const):
- SPEED_OF_LIGHT() -> Velocity { 299792458.0 * 1m / 1s } — c = 299792458 m/s exactly (SI definition).
- BOLTZMANN_CONSTANT() -> Energy / Temperature { 0.00000000000000000000001380649 * 1J / 1K } — k_B = 1.380649e-23 J/K exactly (2019 SI redefinition). Return type as a type expression Energy/Temperature (no J/K dimension alias exists among the 35).
CRITICAL: write the Boltzmann value in DECIMAL form, NOT scientific notation — 1.38e-23 does NOT parse in value position (verified; convention documented at modal_analysis.ri:32-33 and solver_buckling.ri). Doc-comment cites the SI reference. No change needed for pi/g — note that in the task.

PRD: docs/prds/v0_6/stdlib-reconstruction.md task ζ

User-observable signal: examples/stdlib/constants.ri uses SPEED_OF_LIGHT() and BOLTZMANN_CONSTANT() in dimensioned `let`s, compiles with zero Severity::Error and `reify eval` prints c ≈ 2.998e8 m/s and k_B ≈ 1.38e-23 J/K (values matched to the SI definitions). G6 premise verified: c=299792458 m/s, k_B=1.380649e-23 J/K are the exact SI values.
Consumer: a designer using physical constants in loads/energy calcs (CI example); terminal leaf.
Modules touched: reify-compiler (stdlib/units.ri), examples
